prompt: Which compute tier is a `MO_Standard_E4ds_v5` flexible server?
hint: The prefix says it.

choices.text: Burstable
choices.why: That is `B_`.

choices.text: General Purpose
choices.why: That is `GP_`, on D-series machines.

choices.text: Memory Optimized
choices.why: Right: `MO_`, on E-series machines.

choices.text: Business Critical
choices.why: That is a tier of Azure SQL, lesson 8.

prompt: Quitanda gave its PostgreSQL server 512 GB and uses 60. What can it do about the bill for the storage?
hint: Storage grows and does not shrink.

choices.text: Shrink it to 128 GB in place
choices.why: Provisioned storage cannot be made smaller.

choices.text: Nothing in place: a smaller server and a copy
choices.why: Right, which is why the size is chosen for next year.

choices.text: Turn on autogrow, which also shrinks the disk
choices.why: Autogrow only grows.

choices.text: Stop the server, which stops the storage charge too
choices.why: Stopping stops the compute; storage is still billed.

prompt: For how many days can a flexible server stay stopped before Azure starts it again, according to the documentation?
hint: A week.

prompt: `sku_name = "Standard_D2ds_v5"` was refused. What was missing?
hint: Compare it with the declared name.

choices.text: The tier in front, as in `GP_Standard_D2ds_v5`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The number of vCores at the end
choices.why: The `2` in `D2ds` is already the size.

choices.text: A region, since sizes differ per region
choices.why: Region is the `location` argument.

choices.text: Lowercase letters throughout
choices.why: Case was not the issue.

prompt: On a flexible server, what is the administrator login Azure creates?
hint: Not the role the container's `postgres` is.

choices.text: A superuser, like `postgres` in the container
choices.why: It is not a superuser.

choices.text: A member of `azure_pg_admin`
choices.why: Right: it can create databases, roles and allowed extensions, and nothing a superuser alone can.

choices.text: A user with access to one database only, chosen at creation
choices.why: It can create databases.

choices.text: An Entra ID identity, with no password
choices.why: Entra ID sign-in exists, and the declared login has a password.

prompt: The plan said `Buffers: shared hit=15 read=3`. What would a second run of the same query most likely say?
hint: Where did the three pages go after they were read?

choices.text: `shared read=18`, since every run reads from disk
choices.why: Pages read once stay in `shared_buffers`.

choices.text: `shared hit=18`, all of it from the cache
choices.why: Right: the three pages read are now cached.

choices.text: `shared hit=15 read=3` again, since the plan is the same
choices.why: The plan is the same; the cache is not.

choices.text: Nothing, because the result is cached and the query is skipped
choices.why: PostgreSQL caches pages, not results.

prompt: Who applies minor versions, such as 17.5 to 17.6, on a flexible server?
hint: A major version is the other case.

choices.text: You, by starting the upgrade after testing
choices.why: That is a major upgrade, 17 to 18.

choices.text: Azure, in a maintenance window of your choosing
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Nobody: the version is fixed for the server's life
choices.why: Minor versions move.

choices.text: The PostgreSQL community, directly on the server
choices.why: The community publishes releases; Azure applies them.

prompt: In `pg_settings`, what does a `context` of `postmaster` mean?
hint: `shared_buffers` had it.

choices.text: Any session may change it for itself
choices.why: That is `user`, as `work_mem`.

choices.text: An administrator may change it while the server runs
choices.why: That is `superuser`.

choices.text: It is read once, when the server starts
choices.why: Right: a restart applies it.

choices.text: It is set by Azure and cannot be read
choices.why: The container has no Azure, and it read it fine.

prompt: Order the steps that made `pg_stat_statements` answer in the container.
hint: The view refused once, between the first two.

prompt: After `pg_reload_conf()`, `pending_restart` said `t`. What did that mean?
hint: Look at the `setting` column beside it.

choices.text: The new value was applied, and a restart would undo it
choices.why: The setting was still empty.

choices.text: The value is written and read, and waits for the next start
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The server was restarting at that moment
choices.why: It answered the query; it was running.

choices.text: The reload failed and has to be repeated
choices.why: `pg_reload_conf()` answered `t`.

prompt: On a flexible server, how does an administrator get `pg_stat_statements` answering?
hint: The container's way is not available there.

choices.text: `ALTER SYSTEM`, then a restart, as in the container
choices.why: `ALTER SYSTEM` needs a superuser, and the administrator is not one.

choices.text: Editing `postgresql.conf` over SSH
choices.why: There is no shell on the machine.

choices.text: `CREATE EXTENSION` alone, since Azure preloads every library
choices.why: A library still has to be in the static parameter.

choices.text: The server parameter, a restart, and the extension allowed
choices.why: Right: `shared_preload_libraries`, then `azure.extensions` before `CREATE EXTENSION`.

prompt: On a flexible server, an extension has to be listed in the server parameter `azure.___` before `CREATE EXTENSION` accepts it.
hint: The plural of what is being created.

prompt: Which copy protects against a `DELETE` without a `WHERE`?
hint: Both live copies receive the mistake.

choices.text: The high-availability standby
choices.why: It receives the delete before the commit returns.

choices.text: A read replica
choices.why: It replays the delete a moment later.

choices.text: A point-in-time restore to a minute before
choices.why: Right, into a new server.

choices.text: The geo-redundant standby in the paired region
choices.why: There is no such standby; geo-redundancy is for backups.

prompt: Quitanda's analysts run heavy reports at nine. Where should they point them?
hint: Only one of the copies answers queries.

choices.text: The high-availability standby, which sits idle anyway
choices.why: The standby answers no queries.

choices.text: A read replica, accepting that it runs a moment behind
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The primary, through PgBouncer on 6432
choices.why: That pools connections; the reports still load the primary.

choices.text: A server restored every morning from the backups
choices.why: Possible, slower and stale by a day; the replica is the designed answer.

prompt: The declaration with `B_Standard_B1ms` and a `high_availability` block passed `validate`. What happens at creation?
hint: A limit of the cheapest tier.

choices.text: It is created, with the standby on a General Purpose machine
choices.why: Azure does not move a tier for you.

choices.text: It is created without the standby, silently
choices.why: The documented rule is a refusal.

choices.text: Azure refuses: high availability is not on Burstable
choices.why: Right, a rule between two values that only Azure checks.

choices.text: Terraform refuses it at `apply`, before calling Azure
choices.why: The provider accepted the pair in `validate`; the refusal comes from Azure.

prompt: What is the longest backup retention, in days, the provider accepts for a PostgreSQL flexible server?
hint: Its range starts at 7.

prompt: What does an application change to use the built-in PgBouncer?
hint: Same server, another door.

choices.text: Its driver, to a PgBouncer client library
choices.why: PgBouncer speaks PostgreSQL's protocol.

choices.text: The port, 6432 instead of 5432
choices.why: Right, once `pgbouncer.enabled` is on.

choices.text: The server name, to a separate pooler resource
choices.why: It runs on the same machine as the engine.

choices.text: Its SQL, to transaction blocks only
choices.why: Nothing changes in the SQL, though session state needs checking.

prompt: Which of these does the Burstable tier of a PostgreSQL flexible server lack? Choose all that apply.
hint: This lesson met two limits.

choices.text: High availability
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The built-in PgBouncer
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Point-in-time restore
choices.why: Every tier has the backups.

choices.text: Server parameters
choices.why: Every server has them.

prompt: A new application has no engine chosen yet. Which line of the comparison table favours the open-source engines?
hint: Something two columns carry and two do not.

choices.text: The engine is always current
choices.why: That is the SQL Server services' line.

choices.text: They rent an instance
choices.why: They rent a server; the instance is Managed Instance's.

choices.text: No licence in the price
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Their floor is a few DTUs
choices.why: DTUs belong to Azure SQL Database.

prompt: Match each copy of a flexible server with what it is for.
hint: One description on the right belongs to none of them.

pairs.right: a failed machine or zone, with nothing committed lost
reports that may be a moment old
a mistake, undone into a new server
a region lost, restored in its pair

prompt: Quitanda's catalogue runs on a vendor's application that speaks only MySQL, is mostly idle, and is written once a night. Which purchase fits?
hint: The engine decides first.

choices.text: MySQL flexible server on a Burstable size
choices.why: Right: the engine is given and the load is light.

choices.text: Azure SQL Database serverless, which pauses at night
choices.why: The application speaks only MySQL.

choices.text: PostgreSQL flexible server, Memory Optimized, with high availability
choices.why: Wrong engine, and far more than the load needs.

choices.text: A Managed Instance, for the vendor's certification
choices.why: The vendor certified MySQL, not SQL Server.
